findings.evidence: Sentence one: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year." Sentence two: "Specifically, the recommended change is about making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable." Sentence three: "This recommendation removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification."
findings.fix: State the recommendation once, in the specific form (end overdue fines across all ten branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year), and delete or reconcile the vague and absolute restatements so the section leaves only one specification of the ask.
findings.violation: The section titled "Recommendation," the passage the artifact itself presents as its specification of the ask, states the claim three different ways in three consecutive sentences: a specific scoped policy, a vague aspiration with no fixed content, and an absolute broader-sounding version. A reader cannot tell which of the three is the actual ask.

findings.fix: Add an explicit conclusion-signalling phrase at the point the artifact states its central claim, for example "therefore" or "we recommend".
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: No phrase from the conclusion-marker lexicon (therefore, thus, hence, it follows that, we recommend, this paper argues, I argue that, the conclusion is, in conclusion, we should, the case for) appears anywhere in the artifact, so a reader scanning rather than reading straight through has no signpost to where the conclusion is asserted.

findings.evidence: Recommendation section: "Given the return-rate and avoidance-survey results above, the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines..." Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide section: "...the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together, support ending fines for the whole consortium..." No return-rate figures appear anywhere in the artifact; the only pilot data actually given is the avoidance-survey drop from 20 percent to 3 percent, and Circulation Trends describes checkout-volume reporting cadence, not return rates.
findings.fix: Either add the return-rate data the text claims to rely on (before-and-after on-time return rates at the pilot branches) or remove the return-rate reference from both places and rest the claim on the avoidance-survey evidence actually presented.
findings.location: "Recommendation" section, first sentence, and "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, first sentence
findings.violation: The claim's stated grounds cite "return-rate results" twice as though already presented in the artifact, but no return-rate data appears anywhere in it, so half of the cited evidentiary basis for the central claim is not something a reader actually has in hand.

findings.evidence: 10 of 14 sentences (0.71) carry at least one hedging term.
findings.fix: Remove the hedge from sentences whose claim the evidence actually supports, reserving qualification for the claims that genuinely need it.
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: More than 0.35 of the artifact's sentences carry a term from the hedging lexicon (may, might, could, possibly, perhaps, arguably, somewhat, relatively, it seems, appears to, tends to, to a degree), spread across the whole document rather than concentrated where the evidence actually underdetermines the claim.

findings.evidence: Claim: "This recommendation removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification." Grounds: the pilot ran at four of the ten branches, and one of the two evidentiary legs the artifact invokes ("return-rate results") never appears in the document (see the TOULMIN-GROUNDS finding above).
findings.fix: Qualify the recommendation to reflect that it rests on a four-branch pilot, for example "based on results from the four pilot branches" or "pending confirmation at the remaining branches," rather than stating it as unconditional.
findings.violation: The claim is asserted with total certainty and permanence ("without qualification") on grounds that cover only four of the ten branches being committed, part of whose cited evidentiary basis is never actually presented, so a reader acting on this recommendation gets no signal that the result might not generalize to the other six branches.

findings.evidence: Principle: "removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation." Backing offered: the Tri-County brief "reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems that eliminated fines between 2017 and 2022."
findings.fix: Name the source supporting the program-participation half of the principle, for example a citation to the same brief's participation findings if it has them, or drop "and overall program participation" if no such source exists.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, both sentences
findings.violation: The stated principle bundles two effects, increased return rates and increased overall program participation, but the named backing is described only as reviewing return-rate data, leaving the program-participation half of the principle without a named source a reader could check.

findings.evidence: Ending overdue fines is plainly the better path for the consortium, and delaying the change would only cost every branch more.
findings.fix: Either cite data on the cost of delay (for example, projected losses or lost patron participation for branches not yet converted) or remove the cost-of-delay assertion.
findings.location: "What the Pilot Showed" section, first sentence
findings.violation: The assertion that delaying the change would cost every branch more is offered with no evidence anywhere in the artifact, a supporting claim resting on nothing a reader could check.

findings.evidence: It might be that consortium finance records show fine revenue covered under 2 percent of the annual materials budget over the last three fiscal years, and the four pilot branches absorbed the loss without a measurable change to their replacement-copy spending.
findings.fix: State the finance-records figures directly ("consortium finance records show...") and drop the hedge, reserving qualification for claims the evidence does not fully establish.
findings.location: "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section, second sentence
findings.violation: The consortium's own finance records, data the author has direct access to and could state as fact, are hedged with "it might be," understating confidence the artifact's own grounds support and giving a skeptical reader an unnecessary reason to doubt the rebuttal to the revenue objection.

findings.evidence: The section raises and answers only the revenue objection: "a skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall." No passage anywhere in the artifact raises whether results from the four pilot branches can be expected to hold at the six branches never part of the pilot.
findings.fix: Add a passage addressing why the four pilot branches' results should be expected to generalize to the remaining six, for example by naming similarities in patron population or citing the Tri-County brief's coverage of a wider set of systems.
findings.location: "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section, both sentences
findings.violation: The argument raises and answers the revenue objection but never raises or answers the generalization objection its own scope leaves open: whether results from the four pilot branches should be expected to hold at the six branches that were never part of the pilot, a foreseeable challenge to a claim that extends a four-branch trial to a ten-branch systemwide policy.
